description: Assess one one-stop flight connection: does the layover leave enough time to transfer? Use it for a single itinerary; to compare two or more options, use compare_connections once instead of calling this tool for each. Deducts the transfer steps that apply at the connection airport (walking, Schengen passport control, terminal change, security re-screening, baggage re-check) from the layover and returns a decision (recommend / caution / insufficient_data / avoid), a rating (comfortable / reasonable / tight / risky), confidence with reasons, ticket exposure and cited airport facts. Give arrival and departure as local times at the connection airport, or only layover_minutes when that is all the user said. Deterministic and offline: no flight data, no delay prediction. Explain only the returned steps; airport facts apply only where their scope matches the trip.

arrival_terminal.description: Arrival terminal at the connection airport, if known

arrival_time.description: Scheduled arrival of the first flight at the connection airport, local time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm. Give both times, or layover_minutes instead.

baggage_recheck.description: true if checked bags must be collected and checked in again, false if not (hand luggage only, or bags checked through). On separate tickets, leave it out only if unknown: the result then says whether it matters.

departure_terminal.description: Departure terminal at the connection airport, if known

departure_time.description: Scheduled departure of the second flight from the connection airport, local time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm. Give both times, or layover_minutes instead.

from.description: Origin airport of the first flight (IATA), e.g. BER

layover_minutes.description: Scheduled time between arrival and departure, in minutes. Use this when the user gives only a layover duration; do not invent dates or clock times.

terminal_change.description: true if the user knows they change terminals, false if they know they do not. Leave out if unknown: the result then shows the margin with a possible terminal change.

ticket.description: protected = both flights on one ticket/booking; separate = self-transfer on separate tickets; unknown if not stated

to.description: Destination airport of the second flight (IATA), e.g. PVG

name: check_connection

confidence.description: How far the estimate can be trusted, independent of the quality rating. Low means key information is missing.

minimum_connection_minutes.description: A published minimum connection time (MCT), valid only within scope.

decision.description: What to do with this connection. insufficient_data means key information is missing: ask the user rather than recommending it.

if_baggage_recheck.description: Separate tickets with unknown bags: the result if bags must be re-checked.

layover_basis.description: How the layover length was computed: the airport's time zone, explicit UTC offsets, plain clock difference, or a given duration.

mct.description: Published minimum connection times at this airport, separate from the structural estimate. Whether a scoped MCT applies to this trip is unknown, so meets_published does not prove the airline would sell the connection.

possible_steps.description: Steps that may apply but could not be determined. They are not in steps or buffer_minutes; worst_case adds them.

terminal_change.description: unknown: terminals were not given at an airport where changing terminals takes time; see possible_steps.

wall_clock_layover_minutes.description: Present when clocks change during the layover: what the local clocks show.

worst_case.description: The margin if every possible step applies. buffer_minutes is the best case.

title: Check a flight connection
